summary.tldr: Removes minimum penalties for many Criminal Code and drug offences, and changes related sentencing and criminal record rules.
what_it_does: Repeals mandatory minimum penalties for many Criminal Code offences, including some firearms, child sexual exploitation, sexual assault, robbery, extortion and criminal negligence offences.
Replaces several offence sections with only a maximum prison term, often 10 years, 14 years or life, depending on the offence.
Changes some offences involving people under 18, including child pornography, child trafficking and obtaining sexual services, and adjusts related penalties and summary conviction options.
Removes minimum fine rules and other sentencing rules for some impaired driving offences, while keeping or changing treatment program and prohibition order rules.
Removes mandatory minimum penalties for certain drug offences under the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act, and changes related sentencing factors.
Makes related amendments to the Criminal Records Act and other Criminal Code sentencing provisions.
who_it_affects: People charged with listed Criminal Code offences
Victims in sexual and violent offence cases
summary.background: The bill amends the Criminal Code and the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act to eliminate minimum penalties for certain offences. It also makes consequential amendments to the Criminal Records Act.
